title: NEO: Saving GPU Memory Crisis with CPU Offloading for Online LLM Inference
problem: GPU memory limits LLM inference batch size, wasting GPU compute; existing CPU offloading systems either hurt latency (symmetric pipelining bubbles) or require expensive dedicated CPUs.
motivation: Most cloud VMs have abundant DRAM and multi-core CPUs alongside a single GPU. Symmetric GPU-CPU pipelining creates bubbles when GPU stage is shorter than CPU attention. A carefully asymmetric split can keep the GPU fully busy while hiding CPU attention latency.
method: NEO asymmetric GPU-CPU pipelining: each iteration splits into two sub-batches. Batch-0 (all prefill requests + most decode requests) runs a long linear projection stage on GPU. Batch-1 (CPU-assigned decode requests) runs a long attention stage on CPU — both overlap. KV cache split into GPU-cache (HBM) and CPU-cache (DRAM). Layer-wise KV swap overlaps PCIe transfer with GPU compute. Load-aware scheduler uses offline-profiled time models + linear interpolation to greedily assign requests per iteration, comparing GPU-only vs asymmetric pipelining and choosing higher throughput. ISPC-compiled SPMD CPU attention kernels (PACPU) with paged attention, SIMD loads, and Flash Decoding-style parallelism across cores.
key_novelty: Asymmetric sub-batch design that integrates prefill into the GPU batch to extend GPU-stage duration, hiding CPU attention latency and eliminating symmetric pipelining bubbles.
contributions: Asymmetric GPU-CPU pipeline splitting prefill+most-decode to GPU and minority-decode to CPU
Load-aware scheduler with offline time models for per-iteration batch assignment
PACPU: ISPC-based paged CPU attention kernel with SIMD and Flash Decoding parallelism
Layer-wise KV swap to overlap PCIe transfer with GPU linear projection

metrics.speedup: Up to 7.5x throughput on T4, 26% on A10G, 14% on H100 vs GPU-only; up to 79.3% with higher-bandwidth CPUs

limitations: PCIe bandwidth is a bottleneck; gains are largest on low-HBM GPUs (T4) and CPUs with high memory bandwidth
Load-aware scheduler relies on offline profiling; accuracy degrades for unseen request mixes
CPU attention adds latency for long-sequence decode
